summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM deployments scale in 2026, with the market projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Gartner predicts LLM observability investments will account for 50% of GenAI deployments by 2028, up from 15% in early 2026. These tools help teams trace prompts, track token costs, evaluate output quality, and connect AI issues to broader application performance problems.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end LLM application traces, prompt/response chains, token usage, latency, and evaluation metrics across LLM and agent workflows.
features: Deep native integration with LangChain and LangGraph
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month; overage around $2.50 per thousand traces at standard retention; custom Enterprise pricing. (Historically cited around £80/month for higher-volume plans.)
tools.best_for: Teams building on the LangChain/LangGraph ecosystem needing tight tracing, evaluation, and agent testing integration.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests through a gateway/proxy—cost, token usage, latency, caching, and request-level logging across providers.
features: Increasing evaluation and agent monitoring capabilities
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier (10K requests/month); $79/month Pro tier (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); $799/month Team tier (adds SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA); custom Enterprise (SAML SSO, on-prem). Noted as the cheapest simple option (~£20 for 100K requests).
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing simple setup and granular cost tracking/optimization across multiple LLM providers.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: ML experiments, model training, and—via W&B Weave—LLM application traces, evaluations, and production monitoring.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free personal tier for individuals; team/Pro plans are usage- and seat-based; custom Enterprise pricing for larger organizations and on-prem/VPC deployment.
tools.best_for: ML and LLM teams that want unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability in a mature MLOps platform.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML telemetry—performance drift, embeddings, prompt tracing, and online/offline evaluations at enterprise scale.
features: Open-source Arize Phoenix for tracing and evaluation
Extends long-standing ML monitoring expertise to LLMs
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open-source (source-available) for self-hosting; Arize AX (cloud) offers a free tier with paid Pro and custom Enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing robust production telemetry, drift detection, and scalable ML + LLM monitoring.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, prompt management, token/cost tracking, and evaluation metrics, with a strong open-source core.
tools.pricing: LangFuse Cloud free for under 50K observations/requests, then paid tiers (~£20 for 500K); self-hosted free software (~£30/month infra plus ~2 hrs/month maintenance).
tools.best_for: Teams wanting a flexible, open-source-first observability layer with an affordable cloud option and no vendor lock-in.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, vector DB queries, and framework operations via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, exportable to any OTel-compatible backend.
features: Vendor-neutral—export to Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, etc.
Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and frameworks
Traces for prompts, completions, and vector DB operations
tools.pricing: Open-source and free to use; costs depend on the chosen OTel-compatible backend. Traceloop offers a managed platform with free and paid tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams standardizing on OpenTelemetry who want vendor-neutral instrumentation feeding existing observability backends.

cost_tips: Implement response caching for repeated or semantically similar prompts to avoid redundant API calls—tools like Helicone offer this out of the box.
Route requests to the cheapest model that meets quality needs (model tiering/cascading), reserving expensive frontier models for complex tasks.
Optimize prompts and context windows—trim unnecessary tokens, truncate retrieved context, and use concise system prompts to reduce per-request token costs.
Set usage budgets, rate limits, and real-time cost alerts via your observability tool to catch runaway spend before it accumulates.
Batch requests and use streaming where appropriate, and monitor token usage per feature to identify and fix the highest-cost code paths.
